projects.name: Asteria
projects.subtitle: FlightStack & MissionOps
projects.desc: A spacecraft software laboratory, from C++ flight logic to the operator’s console.
projects.problem: Mission software makes more sense when commands, vehicle behavior, fault protection and operator decisions can be explored together.
projects.built: I built a deterministic spacecraft model, integrated it with NASA’s open-source F Prime framework, and connected command and telemetry services to a ground console. The lab includes SAFE-mode protection, guarded commands, six operational procedures, fault injection and journal replay.
projects.proof: The documented local release records 199 automated tests across flight, ground and API layers, 60 mapped requirements, 171 F Prime command-parity frames and 48,708 typed-port channel samples.
projects.scope: An independent educational simulation. The browser demo runs the C++ model through WebAssembly; it does not host the full backend or F Prime deployment. No flight qualification or real spacecraft operation is claimed.

projects.name: A2 MissionLab
projects.subtitle: A mission, reconstructed
projects.desc: An evidence-aware Artemis II explorer connecting trajectory, systems and mission context.
projects.problem: Public mission evidence is scattered across ephemerides, reporting, imagery and technical documents. Understanding a mission requires connecting those sources without inventing missing telemetry.
projects.built: I developed an interactive mission explorer, public-data trajectory analysis, bounded GNC and entry models, a mission library and an evidence-grounded analyst with deterministic retrieval and calculations.
projects.proof: The documented evidence inventory includes 81 public sources, 25 reference datasets, 24 shared mission events and eight deterministic analyst tools.
projects.scope: An independent reconstruction using public evidence. Source data, NASA reporting, derived calculations, models and synthetic examples remain distinct. This is not access to private Orion telemetry or NASA console decisions.

projects.name: C-MAPSS
projects.subtitle: with uncertainty attached
projects.desc: A turbofan remaining-life platform that makes uncertainty part of the interface.
projects.problem: A remaining-life estimate is more useful when an engineer can also inspect its uncertainty, sensor behavior and evaluation assumptions.
projects.built: I built an offline training pipeline and lightweight telemetry path using NASA’s simulated FD001 turbofan data. The system combines bootstrapped tree ensembles, engine-level conformal calibration, schema checks, anomaly flags and an interactive fleet-risk dashboard.
projects.proof: Engine-unit separation prevents rows from the same engine leaking between fitting and calibration. Output-contract tests check RUL caps, uncertainty columns, anomaly fields and evaluation scope.
projects.scope: A research platform on simulated turbofan degradation, not an airline maintenance deployment. The 90% conformal level is a target, not a claim of achieved coverage.

projects.name: GOAT Lab
projects.subtitle: Make the assumptions visible
projects.desc: Jordan or LeBron? A reproducible study of how the answer changes with your values.
projects.problem: “Greatest” depends on what we choose to value. A single ranking can conceal those choices behind a deceptively precise number.
projects.built: I built a transparent multi-criteria comparison with league-relative normalization, peak and longevity measures, playoff context, explicit group budgets and an interactive Streamlit dashboard.
projects.proof: The frozen v1 release includes 250,000 hierarchy-constrained weight simulations, a fixed seed, source and artifact hashes, a model card and 32 release checks. Four alternative scaling choices split the winner 2–2.
projects.scope: The outputs describe selected scaling and value systems. Simulation shares are not objective probabilities of who is the greatest player.

projects.name: Wind VISION
projects.subtitle: Numerics before narratives
projects.desc: Numerical reproduction, a controlled speed study, and a classical baseline that challenged the neural model.
projects.problem: Scientific ML needs both numerical equivalence and physically credible outputs. Faster code is useful only when the comparison isolates what changed.
projects.built: I reproduced constrained latent flow-matching computations in PhysicsNeMo and vectorized an analytical frequency-dependent target. I evaluated held-out synthetic wind reconstruction against classical baselines.
projects.proof: The public final-completion notebook records a four-arm NVIDIA L4 comparison: median full VAE optimizer-step time fell from 268.1946 ms to 48.3596 ms. It records 164 matched VAE gradient tensors and 20 controlled optimizer updates. Original stored figures show the remaining temporal and spectral-fidelity limits.
projects.scope: The public portable release reproduces all eight methods’ metrics from frozen predictions, regenerates three classical baselines from observed sensors only, and matches seven bootstrap intervals. CUDA model inference, training and benchmark timing were not rerun. The complete historical archive remains a separate artifact.
projects.publicEvidence: Public test data, frozen predictions, locked protocol, CPU replay tools and fresh-extraction receipt. Original RC2 model candidate separately included; 108 file hashes verified.

projects.name: Condition monitoring
projects.subtitle: Signals worth investigating
projects.desc: Vibration analysis and alert evaluation that keep generalization limits in view.
projects.problem: High classification accuracy and frequent alerts can look impressive while providing little evidence of future equipment reliability.
projects.built: I built reproducible signal-processing and monitoring notebooks across 40 CWRU bearing recordings and MetroPT-3 compressor telemetry, with source checks, spectral features, chronological evaluation and interpretable review cards.
projects.proof: Bearing balanced accuracy was 97.2% on a held-out-load split and 52.8% on a harder unseen-defect condition. Retrospective compressor comparisons included time-shifted negative controls to expose misleading event matches.
projects.scope: Research and teaching work, not an operational NASA maintenance system. Seeded laboratory faults and four historical compressor events do not establish prospective failure prediction.

roles.summary: Selected for safety-focused AI. Delivering dependable operations software.
bullets: Selected by NASA Langley Deputy Director Allen Kilgore for the Risk-Informed Decision – Deferred Maintenance Tiger Team, investigating human-reviewed AI support for hazard evidence, asset matching and deferred-maintenance feasibility.
Contributed to four fall production application releases within a five-application modernization portfolio, covering relocation, facility closure, safety personnel and environmental review.

Prepared and executed a 69-case safety-personnel verification program across seven suites; re-authored a 55-case environmental-workflow test plan covering permissions, reviews, determinations and notifications.
Verified controlled Oracle / SQL Server write-back behavior across nine Oracle tables and checked facility-closure data parity across 6,459 room records in the test environment.

Authored 25+ test, migration, configuration-management and handoff artifacts across the portfolio, working with process owners and database administrators on release readiness and production feedback.
roles.extra: The Tiger Team assignment concerns a proposed AI Safety Asset Identifier: extracting hazard evidence, matching MAXIMO assets, presenting confidence-ranked findings for expert review and assessing maintenance-data feasibility. Work is scoped as investigation and design. The center context is approximately 200 facilities and 3,400 civil-service / contractor personnel; those are center-wide figures, not application-user counts. Additional research includes Wind VISION and condition monitoring.

roles.summary: Making inference benchmarks useful enough to trust.
bullets: Benchmarked eight model families across vLLM, SGLang and TensorRT-LLM on three GPU classes, producing 102 structured result files.
Automated a result-processing and reporting cycle from 90 to 15 minutes, an 83% reduction for that task.
Identified a workload mismatch that shortened outputs by approximately 77%; corrected comparisons and supported backward-compatible result parsing.

Developed 12 independently reviewable implementation-option pull requests across CLI, configuration, readiness, retry and run-tracking designs, plus a documented engineering handoff; the PRs remained open at handoff.
roles.extra: Beyond the benchmark corpus, I evaluated maintainability and failure behavior through competing implementation options. On Qwen3-32B-FP8 at concurrency 16, the documented comparison was 1,746 versus 1,343 tokens/s for vLLM and SGLang; on Qwen3.6-27B at concurrency 1, TensorRT-LLM versus vLLM time-to-first-token was 1.68 versus 0.26 seconds. These are model/workload-specific findings. The intensive final documented phase ran May–August 2026. Candidate PRs were open at handoff.

roles.summary: Turning disconnected sensor streams into repeatable analysis.
bullets: Integrated five physiological and environmental source families into a reusable 608-row, 41-column daily analysis table.
Normalized timestamps, aggregated observations, aligned features and developed repeatable signal-processing and exploratory prediction notebooks.
Explored cycle and sleep patterns with explicit evaluation and dataset limits.
roles.extra: Research analyses used wearable and environmental observations. They are not clinically validated diagnostic or treatment tools; unsupported noise-reduction and time-savings claims are omitted.

roles.summary: Connecting energy analytics to a human review workflow.
bullets: Worked on a facilities-energy prototype combining a 48-hour XGBoost forecast, PELT change-point detection and Isolation Forest anomalies.
Connected analytical outputs to interactive agent explanations and structured maintenance-review cards.
The prototype demonstration produced 22 review tickets and two proactive recommendations.
roles.extra: A demonstration using mock historical and weather inputs, not a confirmed customer production deployment. The available evidence does not establish sole ownership of every module.
